calls.call: Core in common speech (a Wellspring site) sits beside Essence Core with an explicit aside and its own glossary entry; scholars say Wellspring site and the street says Core.
calls.grounds: The brief keeps both senses of Core and a newcomer would otherwise collide them. The rule that scholars prefer 'Wellspring site' is my wording.

calls.call: One Exchange: corrected the slip. Nell now pushes off her lead foot to his left and goes inside the line of the arm, instead of 'to his left, outside the arm'. The fist passes her left ear.
calls.grounds: A fighter to his left is inside a right-handed straight, and she has to be there to reach his lower left ribs. NATALIE's clarity rule requires the geography to hold. The result of the exchange is unchanged.

calls.call: One Exchange: Judicium's ticking, copper smell and colored lines show during her read at no reserve cost, priced only as the ache behind her eyes.
calls.grounds: The page's reserve accounting has no line for the read, and I did not retype its figures (about 7%, ending near 80%). I treated the read as the stat effect of a harmonization she already holds.

calls.call: One Exchange: the glyph is described as a boundary that held the current to his flank, with no glyph named.
calls.grounds: The Working Card asks for the glyph's boundary condition, the original page named none, and the Glyph Index may not be invented from.

calls.call: The coil stays as the assay instrument, glossed as a great coil of brass a practitioner stands inside.
calls.grounds: The brief says instruments are brass and glass, and other pages in the section use the coil as a fixed term.

calls.call: The Magic System: the car joke (engine, chassis, first corner) became a trebuchet on a hay cart. 'Move the needle' became 'move the reading', and 'honesty meter' became 'plumb line'.
calls.grounds: Motorcars and meters are retired. The joke's point is kept.

canon_conflicts: The other staged pages name the shared arts differently from each other. Coat: Moto *matoi* in How Magic Works and Training and Sects, but *hadagi* in Reinforcement. Kharven 'the hide' in How Magic Works, 'second hide' in Reinforcement. Pressure: Moto *kiatsu* in How Magic Works, *atsu* in Training and Sects. Sensing: *kehai* against *kehai-yomi*. Lineage halls *huti* against *hùtǐ*. My pages use matoi, the hide, gabot, hùtǐ, atsu, the low sky, wēiyā, kehai, nunchi and shénshí, taken from those pages (mostly the majority where they differ). One in ten of a population is already common enough for R83-10, so the figure did not need to change. The four hundred is simple arithmetic, not a new canon number.

calls.call: The Lock no longer closes the first lesson. A new paragraph says the low lesson escaped long ago and there are too many yards to shut. Schedules license, fine and count them, and really guard the next rung: upper manuals, glyph tables, high working and work for pay. The law against teaching a neighbor's son stands and is widely broken. About half a city's yards hold a real license.
calls.grounds: R83-10 (sects and ranks everyone knows) has to coexist with a page about a locked gate. Every schedule, penalty and gate on the page survives. The Five Gates table is unchanged. 'The Imperial Age changed the arithmetic' becomes 'The wars of the Dark Ages changed the arithmetic'.

calls.call: 'Crystal' is sharpened to 'woken Crystal' where a page implied the unawakened have none: On Walking ('Most people standing inside a concentration do not' becomes 'Nine people in ten... do not' have a woken one), Protocol IV's baselines, and Derivation's 'assumes a woken Soul Crystal'.
calls.grounds: The Gate says nearly everyone carries a dormant Crystal, so the old wording contradicted it. The Gate's claim and the one-in-ten figure govern.

calls.call: Proof-marks survive as marks against bolts: 'Bolt and Proof', proofed harness, a stamp naming the house, the bow tested and the range, forged constantly. Grade D's new wording is quoted once.
calls.grounds: The brief retires proof-marks against shot, and R83-5 makes the bolt the cheap killer. Proving armor against a crossbow keeps the section's law and joke without any gun. Isaac may prefer the whole section dropped.

calls.call: The section says 'harness' and never 'plate'.
calls.grounds: R83-4 places full plate in the Imperial Age, and the present tense here is the Dark Ages.

calls.call: Medieval successors are built for the old furniture so its jokes and arguments survive: assay posts for gauge-housings ('the lock is the point'), parish stones for standpipes, searchers for inspectors, snuffers for cutters, Core-tenders for main-men, fee-walkers for meter-readers, a botch for a spur. Assay posts matter because a street's fee hangs on its ground grade.
calls.grounds: The brief says to keep what the page's idea is for: a price, a keeper, an argument and a person to hate. All of these are people or brass and glass with no supply network behind them. Searcher and foreign work are real medieval guild terms.

calls.call: 'The hum' is kept, redefined as the note of kept wards and lamps. Only 'draw-hum' is gone. The stoppage joke is extended: companies repair at three to five in the morning, wardens walk at dusk. The eighty-year and four-minute figures stay.
calls.grounds: The brief retires the draw-hum, not a street's sound. Writing It asks for the hum as room tone.

calls.call: The Bill's figures carry over from What Things Cost: household 3 to 5 and 8 to 12 silver monthly, trade work 2 to 5 gold monthly, searcher 10 to 18 gold monthly (the inspector's wage). The wire's price becomes the beacon line's, a silver for twenty words with addresses counted. New by ear: a bolt costs a copper.
calls.grounds: NATALIE says prices follow the price table and go by ear beyond it. Keeping the numbers lets the Value group convert rows rather than invent new ones.

calls.call: The beacon line inherits the wire's claim to be the first apparatus faster than a horse and its Guild-commodity role. Rail's facts (Transference across a hand's breadth, a line putting towns on somebody's fee) move to the kept road and tuned waystones. The telephone, trams, motorcars, airships and cell-houses are dropped outright as retired. Dye works and 'raise no chimney' stay, as workshops.
calls.grounds: The brief lists rail, wire, telegraph and the rest as gone, and names relays and beacons as the replacement. The beacon line is my own build on that word. Isaac may strike it.

calls.call: Mechanica Part VII is rebuilt around chartered Cores in place of the draw network. Institutional Authorization, the 'engine work with a license on top' charge, the four-hundred-year-old instruments, the two forgeries and the twice-reorganized Division all stay. The term 'engine work' stays, as a built contraption in a cellar. The two-instrument test becomes coil and assay fork.
calls.grounds: The page's argument does not depend on mains. 'Engine' is a medieval word and the page's named practice, and R82-37 allows contraptions.

calls.call: On Walking keeps 'current' as surveyors' word for how a Wellspring's Aether moves through a concentration, with a short note giving R83-9. An aside warns that 'Wellspring Core' on the register means the innermost density class, while common speech calls any worked site a Core.
calls.grounds: The page's title and maxim use the word, and the brief retires only a current in a pipe. The two meanings of Core collide on this page, so I flagged it in voice, not silently.

calls.call: Training and Sects: 'never chosen, and a fighter who names himself is laughed at' becomes 'mostly given by others... laughed at until it works, and then the name is his'.
calls.grounds: R82-5, R82-6 and R82-8: fighters name things, the room laughs until it works, and the most famous name wins.

calls.call: Hedge-workers are written as working by voice, beyond company bounds, paid in kind, on the joke that the schedules have never defined an egg.
calls.grounds: The Four Crafts lists hedge-work among the spoken craft, and The Gate says taking pay without a license is an offense. This is a reading, not a stated rule.

calls.call: Modern phrases swapped: 'bond market' to 'every factor's table', 'counter-intelligence services' to 'the crowns' spy-clerks', 'printed' to copied by sworn scriveners, 'A practitioner is artillery' to 'a siege engine that eats at your table', 'works inscriber' to 'workshop inscriber'.
calls.grounds: R83-4 puts banks in the Imperial Age, and no printing is established.

calls.call: On Standing, Derivation, Walking and Mechanica, many 'it is not X, it is Y' sentences and every em dash were rewritten in place, and British spellings fixed. Every table figure, threshold and DI value is carried unchanged. A wording-level diff of those four pages against the live wiki is worth one read.
calls.grounds: The brief's page rules apply page-wide, and these pages used the banned patterns constantly.

calls.call: Existing mentions of Mu-jin, Niran, Cozbi and Urion's Scale on The Standing and the Title are left as found. No new main-cast material was added anywhere.
calls.grounds: The brief bars new use of the main cast on public pages and also says nothing is lost. These are titles only, with no plot.

calls.call: New fields on every Wellspring entry: Alchemy and Spirit, added before Failure and explained in the hub's How to Read an Entry table. Lines derived rather than on file are marked in-world as '(the trade's reading)' or '(the confessors' reading)'.
calls.grounds: R83-9 and the group note. The markers keep derived lines visibly separate from filed canon. Readings used from file: Alchemetrica (six operations, stage currents), Heresiology glosses, The Four Ceilings substrates, Fracture of Worlds Part Thirteen's 'Temperance through X' lines.

calls.call: Derived alchemy, Caloria. Pyreveil: the Sulfur principle at full heat. Exuroth: the assayer's trial, quench and temper. Ignivale: the first degree of fire. Solfatara: the vessel that breathes. Manganthra: the go-between that stays out of the product. Cataclysm: the vessel's violent end as a law. Pyraeon: the Long Furnace's fire. Catharsis: purgation in the change of state. Penanceflare: the fire that reports itself. Cinerion is on file.
calls.grounds: Each comes from the entry's own Analogue and Failure. Manganthra is deliberately not named as Conjunction's current, because Alchemetrica says Conjunction has none.

calls.call: Derived alchemy, Fulguria. Aurevane: the clear light of the watched vessel. Cymorath: volatile Mercury finding its road up the still. Orrenthal: the metal as a commonwealth. Luminalis: the hidden tincture. Abyntheus: the Emerald Principle at the bench. Judicium is on file (Separation).
calls.grounds: From each law. Abyntheus borrows 'as above, so below' from the Alftian Codex Volume the First.

calls.call: Derived alchemy, Vectoria. Fractura: the assayer's blow. Petralon: Salt in its fixed office. Ascensio: the degrees of fire. Abython: the balanced vessel. Absolution: the gentle reheat. Penance: the hammer's law. Sublimatio and Sublimare are on file.
calls.grounds: From each Analogue. Petralon uses Alchemetrica's Tria Prima, Salt as the fixed principle.

calls.call: Derived alchemy, Spatium. Transference: the tincture shared between two matched vessels. Eclipseron: the dead head read. Transmutatio is on file.
calls.grounds: From each law. Eclipseron uses the caput mortuum from The Real Alchemy.

calls.call: Derived alchemy, Materia. Monolithion: the great casting with no seam. Chthonica: lute, the humble seal. Basilithe: the Standard. Tarturon: a charge carrying its own fire. Terranova: the metal tree in the still flask. Materia Primordia, Coagula, Fixatio and Coagulatio are on file.
calls.grounds: From each law and Alchemetrica's bench vocabulary.

calls.call: Derived alchemy, Vitalia. Anima Spirare: the quickening in the Bed's blood-warmth. Verdantia: the Feeding. Benediction: affinity. Mortalis: the Blacking. Redemption: the sound weld. Contrition: the dose. Phreatis: the remembering menstruum. Rebirthine is on file.
calls.grounds: From each law and Alchemetrica's terms. Contrition uses 'each heals at a measure and poisons past it'.

calls.call: Derived alchemy, Fluxia. Somnalis: the sealed egg before it turns. Thaloré: weight in the vessel. Oblation: the offering in the vessel, the total never rising.
calls.grounds: From each Analogue.

calls.call: Derived alchemy, Limina. Letheveil: the skimming. Lethegraal: the settling. Hypnather: the Standing. Mirithane: the blick. Oneirion: the working in the mind. Eidolyn: the mold. Anamnesis: the fired pot's testimony. Tenebra: the cover-name. Oblivara: the second charge. Nyxial: the Still Bath. Nihiloth: neutralization. Vantabriel: the black that keeps. Dissolution is on file.
calls.grounds: From each law and Alchemetrica's Turnings and apparatus.

calls.call: Derived spirit lines, Materia. Materia Primordia: Temperance through re-forming. Monolithion: permanence. Chthonica: rootedness. Basilithe: constancy. Fixatio: commitment. Coagulatio: settling. Terranova: regrowth. Tarturon and Coagula are on file.
calls.grounds: Fracture Part Thirteen gives 'Temperance through X' for Caloria, Fulguria, Vectoria and Spatium only. These extend the same form from its one-line effect for each Wellspring.

calls.call: Derived spirit lines, Vitalia. Anima Spirare: remembering wholeness. Verdantia: growth. Benediction: grace. Rebirthine: loss. Redemption: being reclaimed. Contrition: a failure owned and survived. Phreatis: memory. Mortalis uses the Heresiology gloss and is unmarked.
calls.grounds: Same method, from Fracture Part Thirteen's one-line effects.

calls.call: Derived spirit lines, Fluxia. Somnalis: uncertainty. Thaloré: depth of feeling. Oblation: sacrifice.
calls.grounds: Same method.

calls.call: Derived spirit lines, Limina. Letheveil: forgetting. Lethegraal: time. Hypnather: rest. Mirithane: self-sight. Oneirion: dreaming. Eidolyn: imagining. Anamnesis: remembrance. Dissolution: unbinding. Tenebra: concealment. Oblivara: keeping one's name against erasure. Nyxial: evenness. Nihiloth: negation. Vantabriel: carrying what was lost.
calls.grounds: Same method. Anamnesis and Tenebra also carry their filed Heresiology wording.

calls.call: Kept 'current' as the trade's old word for a type of Aether, stating that Aether moves over ground as wind moves over a field and that no pipe is involved. Elsewhere in the group a Wellspring is now a 'type', 'Aether' or 'Wellspring'. The glossary gloss 'standing current of natural law' became 'one of the sixty types of Aether, each carrying a fixed law'.
calls.grounds: R83-9 retires the current-in-a-pipe picture. Alchemetrica and other sections still say 'current', and the Density arithmetic rests on Aether crossing a site in about a thousand seconds. 'The Cleansing Current', Absolution's epithet, stays as a fixed name.

calls.call: Replaced 'Denser ground does not help a practitioner' with: denser ground fills him faster and lifts his output ceiling but does nothing for his reach. Every square-root figure stands (an eighteenth, a thousandth, a five-millionth).
calls.grounds: R83-9 and the brief say rich ground fills you faster. The page's own supply column already agrees, and the fall in reach is the part the arithmetic actually proves.

calls.call: Core has three senses, stated openly on the hub: common speech calls any pooling site a Core, surveyors keep 'Wellspring Core' for the top density band (still extraordinarily rare), and Essence Core stays the Crystal layer.
calls.grounds: The brief and NATALIE make a site a Core in common speech. The Density Scale table's top row must survive with its figures. Written as a Measurewright-versus-ferryman joke rather than a silent merge.

calls.call: Density table, 'Where that sits' cell for Active Concentration: 'a charged cell 2,500; cast powder 6,900' became 'a bale of dry straw, burned through, 2,500; a seasoned pine log, burned through, 6,900'. Both numbers are unchanged.
calls.grounds: Cells and powder are retired. The new comparators are computed: straw about 150 kg/m³ at about 16.7 MJ/kg, pine about 450 kg/m³ at about 15.3 MJ/kg.

calls.call: The hub says all sixty carry an alchemical principle, while the six named operations and four stage-lending Wellsprings keep their special standing. The rest are 'no operation filed at the Bench, trade opinion only'.
calls.grounds: R83-9 says the Wellsprings represent alchemical principles. Alchemetrica says six are at once Wellspring, principle and operation, and that Calcination and Distillation are no Wellsprings. This keeps both.

calls.call: Modern-machine images removed from Mechanism fields: turbine blades, laser, 'civilizations set their clocks by quartz', 'a failing conductor flickers a lamp'. Physics terms stay (phase-conjugate mirror, eddy-current inspection, thermite with a gloss, a one-tesla field, Faraday-caged).
calls.grounds: R83: what is built and carried stays medieval, while modern science may explain. The physics was kept and the implied machines were cut.

calls.call: Small non-table prose rewrites beyond retired terms: 'not X, it's Y' constructions and one countdown negation (Thaloré), reworded with facts unchanged, plus 'recopied' and 'sent a reply' for printed and published. Stat Effect text was left untouched apart from spelling.
calls.grounds: The brief's bans and its printing retirement.

calls.call: The coil is kept as a term and re-glossed as a brass assay instrument. Glyph Index class labels changed from 'Derivative — X' to 'Derivative · X'.
calls.grounds: Instruments are medieval, and no em dashes in prose. Counts unchanged.

calls.call: Worked Sentences 'drawing inward' changed to 'running inward'. 'rail' in Descent of Parun stays: it means the Songscript ruling stroke, not a railway. 'Drawn' stays where it means pen or chalk.
calls.grounds: Brief: ordinary 'draw' is fine and the Aether sense is retired. The Lexicon already glosses ma as inward.

The hub says Stat Effect is 'unchanged from the system source'. Left as filed and not resolved here.

The Concordance of Ages: the anonymous later hand, an open-shelf archivist writing below the seal in the last winter before the turn. Also 'the thin' as Ironlink bracket slang for the Withering, and 'arc' as the minstrels' word for a cycle of songs filling one winter.
The Concordance of Ages: 'the split' dated about 740 IC, with rival readings of 738 (Division tax receipts) and 741 (a Dawi hold entry).
The Concordance of Ages: the first blow on the white shelf dated about 310 IC, with the Refusal and the Stay placed there. It is a chronology call on existing Long Reading events.

The Four Ceilings: Master Odo Brandt of the Stannvaard wrights and the Harrow Drag, Year 683: Transference between tuned road-stone and an ore-sledge, ending in the chapel at Ansby.

The Sky, the Hour and the Year: the fight on Stonecrop Fell, Year 671, between Hoshino Tadaie (Moto Sower-watcher) and Perkin Dunmow (Accord chancery), leaving Year 671 with no attested first morning.
The Sky, the Hour and the Year: the Guild hour's new mechanism: the great water clock at Stannvaard, relay riders with sealed sand-glasses, beacons lit at the hinge, and guild hall water clocks.

calls.call: The IC count does not move. Year Zero, First Eon (-1,400 to -900), Antediluvian Calendar (-900 to -450), Reconstruction (-450 to 000), Voyager Era (000 to 070), Long Reckoning (070 to 645), Withering Era (645 to open) and every ceiling date stay as they were.

calls.call: DATE MOVED: the opening of the Imperial Age, 690 IC, is now 800 IC, the turn of the century. It is named only as the Renaissance after the Dark Ages.
calls.grounds: R83-4 supersedes R63-2 and R61-131. 800 is the only century turn most of the cast can reach from 715 (R83-2).

calls.call: DATE RELABELED: 690 IC now opens the Dark Ages, which run 690 to 800 IC. The label takes the old Imperial Age slot, inside the Withering Era. 715 IC stays the sealing year and is now 'the twenty-fifth year of the Dark Ages'. Stamps of 'the Nth year of the Imperial Age' convert by name only, so 700 IC is the tenth year of the Dark Ages.
calls.grounds: The brief sets the Dark Ages as the present tense of these pages. This keeps every stamped year and ordinal on the Alftian, Farrant and Necrocursica pages valid by one mechanical substitution, recorded on the Errata.

calls.call: The present on the wiki stays 715 IC, and Arc One opens about then. For continuity, Chapter One of The Uncounted sits about 715 IC, so Muken is sixteen then. These implied dates are in this report only, not on any page: the forty-year war about 675 to 715, Muken's birth about 699, and the Lorn Stark and Hild Ice era (twenty-two years on) about 737, just before the split.
calls.grounds: NATALIE and the old rulings carry present = 715. TIMELINE.md gives no absolute dates for these scenes, so this contradicts nothing. Isaac may move Chapter One against the count without touching the pages.

calls.call: NEW DATE: Malakar's split of the continents is placed at about 740 IC, near the end of Arc One, with Arc One running about 715 to about 740. Arcs Two and Three run from the split to 800 IC, and I deliberately gave no year for the boundary between them. The page says the minstrels disagree about that joint.
calls.grounds: R83-2, R83-3 and the questionnaire answer 'near the end of Arc 1'. C-164 lists the undated split as a defect. Twenty-five years leaves Muken about forty-one at the split and sixty years for two arcs with time skips. Fixing the Two/Three joint would bind plot R83 does not give.

calls.call: DATE REMOVED: the Traction row's 'from 690 IC, rail on a main' is gone. The Sixth Ceiling now has not fallen. Its Transference law and the 'Year 88' joke survive through the Harrow Drag folly of 683 IC, and the steam-engine line is kept with the array as the reason.
calls.grounds: The brief retires rail, mains, tariffs and Boards, and R82-37 asks for contraptions that misfire. A failed attempt keeps the law and the argument.

calls.call: C-164 NOW READS (proposed Status text, for the launching session to log): 'Ruled 2026-11-05 by Isaac on the order: Muken lives before the split and survives it; Malakar splits the continents near the end of Arc One. Agent ruling (Natalie, wiki rewrite): the Concordance dates the split about 740 IC and treats the whole IC count up to then as the Grand World. The Long Reading's split in II to IV is read as a first blow on the white shelf about 310 IC, which the Moto registers call the split: the Reading of it, the Refusal and the Stay fall there, the Long Diminishment follows, and the Recension stays two to four generations before Muken. The great split proper comes after Muken. Kharven-Seat already stands before Muken and he takes its crown rather than building it. The Long Reading, The Moto Bloodline, The Moto Origin and the Kharven page are to be revised to this. Status: ruled, pages pending.'
calls.grounds: The Long Reading itself says the eye gives pressure and no hour, and the Stay needs a blow to answer. 310 IC comes from its 'four centuries' of Holy Sea testimony counted back from 715. A two-stage break keeps every Moto event while obeying R83-3 and the book, where a person can still walk the Grand World. Reading Order says the Seat and the Foot already stand. Isaac overturns this by striking one paragraph in Concordance Section VI.

calls.call: The 'first blow' on the shelf is left unattributed on the page: the later hand holds it was the same hand as the split, and two Measurewrights file it as a coastal collapse.
calls.grounds: R83-3 names Malakar for the split only. R83-11 lets scholars argue.

calls.call: Vantage: everything above the seal keeps its 715 present. The arcs, the split and the Imperial Age appear only in Concordance Section VI and one marginal note in the Errata, in an unattested later hand writing in the last winter before the turn, which is still the Dark Ages. On this group's pages the arcs appear only in the Concordance.
calls.grounds: A document sealed in 715 cannot know 740, but the brief requires the Concordance to place them. A hand before the turn keeps the Dark Ages as present tense and names the Imperial Age only as what comes after.

calls.grounds: NATALIE's tone bans a gray reading of the setting. The name needed a loud origin and a witnessed first year, because the Guild 'dates an age from its first witnessed year'.

Essence supply becomes Core-keepers' contracts, crews on retainer and sealed Holding vessels on mule-back. Conduit survives only over the length of a pit or curtain wall. The ninety-hour drowning, the famine, the Withering and 'Essence traders that happen to own holes' are all kept.
calls.grounds: The brief retires mains and tariffs and says nothing is lost otherwise. R83-8 has living people who can refuse. The brief also says a worked Core recharges and its keepers can close it.

canon_conflicts: The Long Reading II to VI and its Open Rulings ('two to four generations before Muken', 'twenty-fifth year of the Imperial Age', 'the rest of the body of the world came apart around it') still read as a completed split before Muken. They conflict with the Concordance Section VI and need the first-blow revision in the C-164 text.

The Moto Bloodline and The Moto Origin have Malakar's splitting scatter the seven lines and Muken build Kharven after it. Reading Order and the book have the Seat and the Foot already standing, and the split comes later.

The Moto Bloodline says Muken was removed and 'died to a dirty one', and Yukazuri's card has been read as outliving him. R83-3 requires him alive through the split, about 740 IC. I gave no death on these pages.

Sohai, The Whole Bow defines the Okuchi as 'the body of the world before Malakar broke it', which every other people named after the disaster. On the new order that world is still standing in 715. The Sky page now glosses the Okuchi as 'the deep old country of the Moto reading' and drops 'outlived the Okuchi' for 'outlived the stations'.

The book's 'Before' has the Archons and Titans fighting a forty-year war that ended a month before Chapter One, and Reading Order says 'one war, forty years long'. R83-6 and The Four Ceilings treat the Great Spirit War as ancient and off the count. Whether they are one war is not settled. These pages keep the Great Spirit War undated and do not mention the forty-year war.

Quarter names 'Old World' and 'New World' remain in use before the split. I treat them as names of quarters of one continent, but Geography pages may describe seas between the quarters and need checking against the Grand World.
